notes.title: Glitchhikers Second Anniversary Patch!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/d4c9afe89e6d0871047d21b3a8965c19a66f2bd2.png[/img]

Happy April Fools Day, to one and all—or as we'd like to rename it, "The Fool's Day." This is not a trick and we have no desire to deceive! In 2024 our communities do not need a special day to celebrate social deception. So instead of delighting in corporations blatantly lying to you, albeit with a little more twinkle in their eye than usual, let's celebrate the positive aspects of foolishness!

In tarot, the fool is a special and significant card. It marks the beginning of an epic journey, when all things are still possible. It also signifies a beginner's mind, in which the humble acknowledgement of ignorance allows for openness, eagerness, and a lack of preconceptions. Every day we all are fools in many ways and in many subjects, and we are all fools at the mercy of modern systems beyond our total comprehension.

And of course, this also marks the 2-year anniversary of the release of Glitchhikers! Thank you for being with us on this amazing journey—the game continues to get better in small and subtle ways based on player feedback. Our achievement hunters were suffering as they tried to find every single character in the game, so we've made some changes to the way the hikers spawn that will [b]much more strongly favour new encounters[/b] until they have all been exhausted through repeated journeys. If you’re just missing a few hikers, or if you’re starting the game for the first time, this new patch should help ensure more varied and unseen parts of the game!

(If you’re still having trouble finding certain hikers to fill out your Cool Zone, be sure to check out [url=glitchhikers.com/cool-zone]our full hiker breakdown on the Glitchhikers website,[/url] which lays out which hikers can be found where, and whether they have certain conditions before appearing in the game.)

Thanks again for being with us these last two years. May we all be the fool today and open our minds to new experiences and journeys, together.

[h3]Full Patch Notes[/h3]
1.0.9
General:
- Greatly increases the chance of spawning hikers that have not yet been encountered on a given journey

notes.title: Glitchhikers Nominated at CIGAs 2023
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/6df4cfe4320a38e06ec36ee483368c03ae001914.png[/img]

Hey there Glitchhikers fans!

We've got some super exciting news to share with you today - Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between has been nominated for not one, not two, but SIX awards at the 2023 Canadian Indie Game Awards happening tonight in Toronto! How awesome is that?!

We've been nominated for Best Studio, Best Debut Indie Game, Best Art Direction, Best PC Game, Best Score/Soundtrack, and Best Narrative. We couldn't be more proud of the entire team who poured their heart and soul into this project.

We couldn't have done it without your support, so we wanted to say a huge thank you to all of our fans who have played, shared, and championed Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between. Your enthusiasm for our little indie game means the world to us!

If you would like to watch the ceremony it will be streamed live on Twitch tonight at 7pm ET/ 4pm. [url=https://www.twitch.tv/cgameawards]You can watch it here.[/url]

We'll be sure to keep you all updated on how we do at the awards ceremony. Fingers crossed for some wins, but just being nominated alongside so many other amazing indie games is a huge honor.

Thanks again for all your support, and we'll see you out there on the digital highways and byways!

notes.title: Getting To Know the Hikers #1
notes.notes:
Our Hikers can be a bit mysterious. They don't have names (though we love hearing players' names for them), and we don't like giving them backstories that aren't discoverable in the game through conversation. Each Hiker definitely has their own personality, interests, and vibe though. We'd love to introduce them to you!

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/ebbd740145b85887cde7b418712c16af/898826089833a0cd-e5/s1280x1920/e22927bbfeaa84ef4ebac4478617ccfbdf5da33d.pnj[/img]

A good place to start would be with the first Hiker we modelled for Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between. They were an entirely new Hiker (not one of the 6 Original Hikers featured in First Drive). As you may glean from their kin list here, this Hiker has a love of the natural world and science, but one that they'd rather experience through a glowing monitor than in person. 


[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/ecf40bd9928fbea1182ee834a6d934fd/898826089833a0cd-29/s1280x1920/358592eb612e1063e499083c2fccf02978b377b8.gifv[/img]

Still, being so intimately connected to technology means that they are acutely aware of the pitfalls, problems, and outstanding questions that all of our technological advances leave us with. They'd love to get your take on it all, if you find them for a chat during commercial breaks.

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/8f7fee4686aefbd8c7cedf8afc3c88a8/898826089833a0cd-2b/s1280x1920/bd6042f4b2ae1176a600134180b1db8fc8492d18.pnj[/img]

In their earlier design, we considered giving them a bit more of a volatile temper.  In the original design, along with the yelling animation, this Hiker was to have an inner ring of rotating teeth that you would see when staring down their lens.  

We'd hate to add to negative cyborg stereotypes though, so later iterations had more of a subtle kind of snark than rage-filled murderbot vibes.

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/fcf12619da23316181ba92668533d383/898826089833a0cd-d0/s1280x1920/d01a0fa3a9d6ed4a5558311befc312af3ee3bd11.pnj[/img]

As you've probably noticed, one of this Hiker's defining features is the retro TV that they have for a hand. They use this device in the ways most of us use our cellphones; to learn, to connect with people, to watch their nature documentaries, and as a multipurpose tool like a flashlight, a beacon, and a mirror. 

Some more subtle features would be the comfy grey blanket they wrap around themselves over their PJ pants and black shirt. Their face is a camera lens.

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/56d872828a03671b0a9f229524c55835/898826089833a0cd-b2/s1280x1920/41fc1ba89faf6422fad63aab167d3e2c856690dc.pnj[/img]

As they were the first character that we generated a 3D model for, their design was where we really figured out the lowpoly style of Glitchhikers. Starting out with this very smooth plastic look, we decided on a need for more texture and geometric elements. 

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/d6610d112a0a835ed83756d8b9669766/898826089833a0cd-77/s540x810/57afa04dcb734c1ec9921becf7b701a2cae26df8.pnj[/img]

Along with the general environments of Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between, the characters were remade into this triangle-heavy geometric figures. 

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/6388634b98465e3603d7605e1160c803/898826089833a0cd-26/s1280x1920/3b3243bc50866a8d73333571abaed41a1f1b94fc.pnj[/img]
[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/7a5a618d84d4b26224cc8f6cc71b3654/898826089833a0cd-79/s1280x1920/c237e64846f2a7246a938affb93a2bd92a0e996d.pnj[/img]

We also had some ways to go to figure out the final look of the glitching that occurs throughout the game. We wanted the atmosphere of the game to be chill and inviting, while still surreal and dreamlike. Some of the earlier attempts definitely fell on the "horror" or unsettling side of the line though.

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/cb5034d8a5018aa24439f3dd45bd468f/898826089833a0cd-c9/s1280x1920/59643f2b61dee58a360a7dd3b9ae0a79480bc8c0.pnj[/img]

Here is their Agender pride flag poster that we first tweeted out for Pride month 2022. 

[img]https://64.media.tumblr.com/5a1f6fa986dc24a2151ebeb99ee9c4df/898826089833a0cd-db/s1280x1920/f93b57932c515d3ed5b918d49489df8c9247a6b8.pnj[/img]

You can meet this Hiker on The Highway, The Path, or The Terminal. Keep your eyes peeled for the glowing screen of their hand.

notes.title: Silverstring's 2022 Round Up
notes.notes:
Happy 2023 [i]Glitchhikers[/i] Fans! For those of you who may have missed our end-of-year studio round up on Twitter, we thought we would catch you up on some of our [url=https://silverstringmedia.com/news/2022/12/16/silverstrings-2022-round-up-a-year-of-growth-and-good-fortune]2022 highlights[/url], and look at the road ahead.

We feel unbelievably blessed for all of the success and support we've had in the last year. So much of that has come directly from this community taking a chance on a game about strange starlit journeys and curious Hikers. 

We've had the chance to connect with a lot of you during livestreams, in the Discord and [url=https://linktr.ee/slvrstrng]across social media[/url], and at conferences virtual and in person. We've been touched by your reviews and thoughtful articles from games outlets big and small. 

[url=https://silverstringmedia.com/news/2022/4/18/glitchhikers-music-monday-roundup]On the musical side[/url], we released some [i]Glitchhikers [/i]music videos, shared our influences in a series of themed Mix Tapes, and had the entirely surreal experience of [url=https://silverstringmedia.com/news/games-in-action-2022]watching a live orchestral performance[/url] of a medley of [i]Glitchhikers[/i] songs. 

Our team has grown in number and skill, beginning work on new prototypes that build on everything we learnt from [i]Glitchhikers[/i], and wandering into entirely new stories, art styles, and genres. [url=https://silverstringmedia.com/news/2022/12/16/silverstrings-2022-round-up-a-year-of-growth-and-good-fortune]You can read more about our year on our blog.[/url]

While we're moving ahead on exciting new projects, we've still got Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between on our minds. You can expect our continued support and more announcements to come, particularly as we get closer to our one year anniversary on March 31st. Be sure to follow us on[url=https://www.tumblr.com/silverstringmedia] Tumblr,[/url] [url=https://twitter.com/Slvrstrng]Twitter[/url], and [url=https://bit.ly/SSMSubscribe]subscribe to our newsletter[/url].

This game is designed to be timeless, to be here for you whenever you need it. It's a reminder that you can take space for yourself, that you can let your mind wander. It's a friendly hand reaching out from the void. It's permission to look at yourself and the world, to pull on the threads that connect us all, to untangle the knots and begin to weave together the future you want. Whether you play it once, or you return many times, we thank you for being open to the journey.

Thank you for travelling with us. More journeys await.

notes.title: Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between review: a good walk ruined
notes.notes:
I was out with friends once and a person who was a mutual aquaintance with a pal, and who did something or other in theatre, looked at a couple of us with sad eyes and asked "What have you been doing recently to give your life meaning?"

I think your reaction to the idea of someone asking you that will predict your response to Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between, a self-described "surreal journey through the spaces between places". Do you think "what have you been doing to give your life meaning?" is a cool way to start a conversation? A better prompt than you'd normally encounter? A big question, rather than small talk? Then you will probably be more open to the delights of Glitchhikers, a game where where you talk about choice and predetermination to what appears to be sentient windchimes while driving along a one-way motorway. Where you take a nighttime walk around a park peopled with meditating animals who have opinions about magic.

Read more

notes.title: The Music that Makes Glitchhikers
notes.notes:
Whether we are talking about [url=https://silverstring.itch.io/glitchhikers][b]Glitchhikers: First Drive (2014)[/b][/url], or [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1449230/Glitchhikers_The_Spaces_Between/][b]Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between[/b][/url], one thing is certain—the Glitchhikers Experience cannot be separated from the strange and unforgettable in-game music. Fans old and new will invariably point to the original soundtrack as the siren song that drew them into the world, made them comfortable to sink into the surreality, and brings them back time after time. 

When we sat down to make The Spaces Between we knew that building upon the 6 song First Drive OST was going to present an exciting challenge. The Glitchhikers sound is so particular yet so difficult to nail down. It is in many ways an amalgamation of mangled pieces of several genres, held together by a membrane of synth-laden loops. Each one is more than the sum of its parts, like musical mosaics constructing a full picture out of shattered fragments of songs. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/39a08c9af49ee4261d38c7f9b09824789516cae0.png[/img]

To give you a deeper look into our journey recreating and reimagining this alchemic magic, we went directly to the source -- Devin Vibert, Silverstring’s Musical Lead and composer of the songs of both First Drive and The Spaces Between. 

[i][h3]Can you tell us what makes a Glitchhikers song? What are you hoping for when you sit down to create one?[/h3][/i]

The music in Glitchhikers and Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between is meant to be a little weird, a little broken, and at times a little beautiful. A lot of the music is very ephemeral; songs will drift between (or use simultaneously) seemingly disparate styles or moods. This is much like some of the interactions a player will have: a strange hiker has an interesting and often meandering conversation with them, before they disappear into the night or the player moves on.

Above all else, the music is meant to be meditative—like many of the other design aspects of the game, it’s meant to leave space for the player to have whatever experience they’re prepared to have. That said, I very much wanted to (at risk of using a hackneyed term) play with liminality in the music, and so a lot of the songs are built from these weird bits of musical flotsam and jetsam. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/4d2a34a48e35223767823e3c0132d446a1721cd8.jpg[/img]

[i][h3]Did you pull this concept from the ether or were you drawing inspiration from something? Did you have any guiding stars?[/h3][/i]

Both [Claris Cyarron, Creative Director and Collaborating Composer] and I have looked to [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Disintegration_Loops]The Disintegration Loops[/url] as a source of inspiration for this type of “audio-destruction-turned-pretty” aesthetic, and you can hear it all over the place. A song might, for example, start with a badly distorted loop ripped from an earlier version of a different song stuck with a melody made by a malfunctioning synth patch that drifts into a reverb-soaked piano and an acoustic guitar part that has been so badly time-stretched that it’s riddled with audio artefacts. There were some other songs and artists that have inspired the music of The Spaces Between, and I have put together [url=https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLwWmZgzJR6bSPViKJLRlDn25H_JU-ZUO3]a playlist of sorts on YouTube highlighting[/url] the, er, most telling ones. 

[i][h3]Is there a particular connecting thread to these songs that you are most drawn to? What gives something the spirit of a Glitchhikers song across genres or structural differences?[/h3][/i]

A lot of the best (imho) parts of the soundtrack are those songs where several seemingly busted pieces of audio are smashed together to create something actually musically coherent; I leaned hard into a lot of lo-fi sounds. Sometimes I intentionally time-stretched audio using the wrong algorithms and then would challenge myself to make it sound cool and interesting. If I was having trouble with a song, I’d cannibalize an unused (or already-used, I didn’t mind!) section from another track and process it to the point where it was barely recognizable, and use it to blow the creative block wide-open. Some melodies are completely improvised and were recorded in a single take and never altered.



[i][h3]The Spaces Between was a much larger undertaking than the shorter, tighter experience of First Drive. To compare, First Drive had one journey mode and 6 songs total, while The Spaces Between has four main modes and a whopping 5-Volume, 71 track Deluxe OST.

Could you give us some insight into your process for each journey, starting with The Highway (the most similar mode to First Drive)?[/h3][/i]

We wanted to cleave pretty closely to what we did in OG Glitchhikers, which was for the music to be a little unsettling and broken, but for it to still manage to be somewhat chill and meditative—a tricky line to walk. The music also needed to stay out of the way of the conversations the player would be having, so early on it was decided that these songs would be light on lyrical content and should be able to play in the background without being particularly disruptive. We did want to expand the repertoire of the Drive music a bit, adding elements of jazz, lo-fi, and lounge whilst still hanging on to the chopped-up-and-shuffled audio aesthetic that made it what it was in the OG.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/f3e675c627cc9da7c74092c079968f674bd81c90.png[/img]

[i][h3]The Path mode (where players are free to walk through many winding paths of a park with music being delivered using a “Glitchpod”) is a pretty different thematic and mechanical experience to The Highway. How did that influence your approach?[/h3][/i]

The Path necessitated a different approach to composition—you’re listening to songs between segments of a podcast, and so the music is the sole focus of the audio experience (unless you turn your GlitchPod off, which I recommend everyone do on occasion because silence is also nice, and I find the ambience of the Path very soothing!). For the reasons above, and because the Path is decidedly a more active experience than the Highway, we wanted the music to be more upbeat, convey a stronger sense of wonder and intrigue, focus on nature/the living world, and to generally inhabit “the present”. Thus, many of the songs for the Path journey have lyrics, stronger melodies, a faster tempo, and very generally use a lot more transients (“fast” sounds like a clap or plucked strings) when compared to songs for the Highway.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/0e9dec8dcf7be81b4b9aab0a3413750be565f66d.jpg[/img]

[i][h3]The Railway is a journey that we've described as more communal and warm. It has the most in common with The Highway in many respects, but musically is probably one of the bigger departures from First Drive. Tell me about your thought process for that?[/h3][/i]

Pretty much by default, the Railway journey was going to require an atypical approach to the music. Trains don’t normally blare radio music throughout, but without any music it would feel a bit empty. Almost right from the start of development we were into the idea of a busker lightly playing music in each train car, but we wanted to ensure this didn’t get grating to the listener after a little while. From this blossomed the idea that in each car, the busker would be playing different instruments, and different parts of the same song. Since the sound bleeds through from adjacent cars, you’d hear multiple copies of the busker harmonizing or playing along with each other in a disjointed, multiple-train-car jam session.

The intent was for the railway to be a safer and more comfortable space than with the other journeys, so it was decided that the music would have a warmer, more organic feel than the other journeys. There are virtually no synths, (though in-game the busker technically is using a synthesizer to play string and brass samples sometimes), and most of the instrumentation should feel pretty familiar to most folks—guitar, drums, bass, piano, strings, brass, nothing too crazy. (I did use an aluphone a bunch too, but shhhh) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40379897/40336ad01f443e5f0807d3a7ab0cefc57d23d519.png[/img]

[i][h3]You've spoken before about The Terminal mode as being the one with the most control, both in terms of absolute freedom for players to explore the environment, and in terms of musical control. In some ways it is the least First Drive-like mode, and yet it takes the spirit of musical experimentation and the stitching together of disparate and broken sounds to its extreme. How would you explain it?[/h3][/i]

The music in the Terminal is this ethereal, looping vapourwave behemoth that slowly morphs, adding and removing parts and instruments depending not just where in the space the player travels, but how they do it as well. Effectively Claris and I wanted to have the entire Terminal function as a giant, bespoke player-controlled synthesizer, where their actions (and a few procedural things) could affect the sound just as someone might twist a filter knob or punch in a loop. The hope was that folks would find enjoyment just in playing around with these sounds as they also played around in the space. The Hikers we encounter in the Terminal also act as mini-synths: each one emits looping melodies unique to their personality that can change depending on a variety of different player actions/choices.


With that, we decided to wrap the interview and leave more musical mysteries and surprises for players to uncover for themselves when Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between drops March 31st for PC, Mac and Nintendo Switch (you can find information on available platforms on the newly redesigned [url=http://www.glitchhikers.com]glitchhikers.com[/url]). The 22-track OST and the 5-volume Deluxe Soundtrack that contains all 71 in-game songs will also be available from Day 1 as part of bundles, with more outlets TBA. Until then, you can find the three singles that have been released on [url=https://devinvibert.bandcamp.com/music]Devin’s Bandcamp[/url], with official Music Videos available on [url=https://www.youtube.com/c/SilverstringMedia]Silverstring Media’s YouTube[/url]. 

[h3]To hear more from Devin and Claris about the Sights and Sounds of Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between you can [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RPbb11bMHVg]watch their showcase from Steam Next Fest[/url]. [/h3]

Where will the journey take you? Find yourself along the way.

Taking inspiration from the experimental and critically-acclaimed 2014 alt-game, [i]Glitchhikers: First Drive[/i], the reimagined and reborn [i]Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between[/i] expands that slice of surreality to reach entirely new horizons. [i]Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between[/i] will be launching on PC and Mac in early 2022. 

In a free-form narrative defined entirely by the player, [i]Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between[/i] ensures every playthrough is unique through randomized encounters with up to 18 mysterious characters. Each conversation will prompt personal reflection and rumination, guiding each player to thoughtfully consider themes of life, death, and the cosmic sublime in how they connect with their own lives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33025617/cb88f200a7b0e435594c474f1be5a630fd3cf389.png[/img]

Glitchhikers: The Spaces Between will be the first major game by Silverstring Media, who have worked on a number of critically acclaimed independent games including Celeste, Wandersong, Manifold Garden, and Where the Water Tastes Like Wine.
